events.title: Execution of William Wallace
events.description: Scottish knight William Wallace, a leader of the Wars of Scottish Independence, was hanged, drawn and quartered in London after being convicted of treason by King Edward I of England.
events.significance: Wallace became a lasting symbol of Scottish resistance and national identity, and his martyrdom helped inspire Robert the Bruce and the continued struggle for Scottish independence.

events.title: British Forces March on Washington
events.description: During the War of 1812, British troops under Major General Robert Ross defeated American forces at Bladensburg on August 24 after beginning their advance toward Washington, D.C., on August 23, leading to the burning of the capital.
events.significance: The burning of Washington, including the Capitol and the White House, was the only time a foreign power has captured and occupied the US capital, and it spurred American resolve and later the defense of Baltimore.

events.title: Execution of Sacco and Vanzetti
events.description: Italian-born anarchists Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti were executed in Massachusetts for the 1920 murders of a paymaster and guard during a robbery in South Braintree.
events.significance: The case sparked worldwide protests and became a symbol of alleged injustice, xenophobia and political prejudice in the American legal system; in 1977 Massachusetts Governor Michael Dukakis proclaimed that they had not been treated justly.

events.title: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact Signed
events.description: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression treaty in Moscow, accompanied by a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of influence.
events.significance: The pact cleared the way for Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, and the start of World War II in Europe, and the Soviet occupation of the Baltic states and eastern Poland followed.

events.title: The Baltic Way
events.description: About two million people joined hands to form a human chain stretching roughly 675 kilometers across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania on the 50th anniversary of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.
events.significance: The peaceful demonstration drew world attention to the Baltic states' demand for independence from the Soviet Union, which they regained in 1990-1991.
